Description: Infection of susceptible individuals who become asymptomatic carriers, through exposure to contaminated water.
Infection of susceptible individuals who develop symptomatic cholera, through exposure to contaminated water.
Successful vaccination of susceptible individuals, conferring immunity.
Recovery of asymptomatic individuals, who then become immune.
Recovery of symptomatic individuals, who then become immune.
Waning of immunity acquired from natural infection, returning individuals to the susceptible population.
Waning of vaccine-induced immunity, returning individuals to the susceptible population.
Transition of bacteria from the hyperinfectious state to the less infectious state.

Name: β
Description: Rate of 'contact' with reservoir water, representing the maximum infection rate from less-infectious bacteria.

Name: γ
Description: Per capita recovery rate from cholera infection, reciprocal of the duration of infection (2.9 to 14 days).

Name: δ
Description: Removal rate of cholera bacteria from the water reservoir, reciprocal of the cholera life span in water (3 to 41 days).

Name: ξ
Description: Rate of water contamination by an infectious person.

Name: κ
Description: Concentration of cholera that yields a 50% chance of infection (half-saturation constant).
